change.description: feat(mobile): animated mascot screen offering a downloaded OTA update
change.author: Prasad-D-Ware

findings.title: Resume route is consumed at launch but applied after an unbounded wait, and can replace the page the user navigated to
findings.body: `takeResumeRoute()` deletes the record and checks the 2-minute age at launch (updateResumeStore.ts:38-43), but the navigation happens only once `config !== null` (line 44). `config` stays null whenever the selected machine does not answer: `resolveActiveConfig` returns null for an unreachable or failed host (resolveConfig.ts:55-60), and the store sets `config` to null on every backgrounding (store.tsx:654). So with the machine offline or slow, the age limit is never checked again. When the machine answers later, even minutes later, `restoreAction` runs against whatever page the user is on by then. If they have opened another page, it returns "replace" and that page is swapped for the saved one. The user gets an unexpected jump or loses their place, with no error. This contradicts the doc on `RESUME_MAX_AGE_MS`, which says a saved page must not reopen later as a surprise. Fix: keep the record's `at` and drop the restore once it is older than `RESUME_MAX_AGE_MS` when the effect finally runs. Also only "replace" when the user has not navigated since launch. The `replace` branch exists for the stale deep link that expo-router reopens after a reload (updateResume.ts:63-67), so keep it for that case.

findings.title: applyUpdate is not re-entrant: a double tap on Restart reloads twice
findings.body: `applyUpdate` always sets `restarting`, sleeps, and calls `reloadAsync`, even when a restart is already under way. The Restart button (UpdateScreen.tsx:92-97) only becomes non-pressable (`pointerEvents="none"`, line 89) after React re-renders from the store change. A second tap in that window starts a second `applyUpdate`. That runs `reloadIntoUpdate` twice, writing the resume record and calling `Updates.reloadAsync` twice. If the reload fails, the first rejection hides the screen while the second call is still pending. `showUpdateReady` and `dismissUpdateScreen` already ignore calls while restarting. Make `applyUpdate` return early the same way, or share the in-flight promise.

findings.title: iOS screen readers can still reach the visually hidden Restart / Not now buttons
findings.body: While restarting, the buttons are hidden with `opacity: 0` and `importantForAccessibility="no-hide-descendants"` (lines 88-91). The same prop hides the progress block while ready (line 78). `importantForAccessibility` only applies on Android. On iOS, VoiceOver can still focus the invisible buttons and activate "Not now", which does nothing during a restart. Add `accessibilityElementsHidden={restarting}` to the actions container and `accessibilityElementsHidden={!restarting}` to the progress block, next to the existing props.

findings.title: "never reloads on its own" test cannot fail
findings.body: `reloadAsync` is created on line 33 but never passed to anything. `showUpdateReady` and `dismissUpdateScreen` take no reload API, so `expect(reloadAsync).not.toHaveBeenCalled()` on line 36 always passes, whatever those functions do. The no-reload guarantee actually comes from `applyUpdate` being the only function that takes a `ReloadApi` (`updateScreenState.ts:61`). Either delete the test or assert something observable. For example, assert that after `showUpdateReady()` the phase is still `ready`, and that no `restarting` state was ever published to a subscriber.

contracts.action: Restart now goes through reloadIntoUpdate: save the current page, then Updates.reloadAsync (UpdateScreen button and the Settings row)
contracts.equivalent_path: Before this change the Settings row called Updates.reloadAsync() directly (settings/index.tsx) and UpdatesManager called it on resume, with no saved page and no screen. Both now go through applyUpdate({ reloadAsync: reloadIntoUpdate }).
contracts.before_after: Before: reload went to the root route and the user landed on the board. After: the page is saved in AsyncStorage, the restarting screen is held 900 ms, then the reload runs. The resume-on-foreground reload is gone. A downloaded update now only raises the screen.
contracts.visible_effect: The user sees the mascot screen, then "Restarting…", then the app reopens on the saved page.
contracts.failure_mode: If the save fails, the app reopens on the board (swallowed on purpose). If the reload rejects, the saved key is removed, the screen is hidden and the error is logged with console.warn, so the app stays usable. A double tap can run this twice (reported as a finding).

contracts.action: On launch, read and delete the saved resume route, then push or replace it once navigation and config are ready
contracts.equivalent_path: The onboarding.ts / onboardingStore.ts split named in updateResume.ts. A deep-link restore by expo-router also reopens the last link after a reload.
contracts.before_after: Before: nothing was restored after a reload. After: the record is read and deleted at mount, and navigation waits for `navState.key` and a non-null `config`.
contracts.visible_effect: The saved page opens over the board, or replaces a stale deep-linked page. If `config` stays null the page never opens.
contracts.failure_mode: `takeResumeRoute` swallows read and remove errors and returns null, so an unreadable store only skips the restore. Nothing is written back from that read, so the empty-on-error pattern does no harm here. The record is deleted before it is used. If `config` stays null for a long time, the restore fires late or never, and the age check is no longer applied (reported as a finding).

contracts.action: UpdatesManager raises the update screen when a download lands (shouldOfferUpdate effect) and again after 15 min in the background
contracts.equivalent_path: The old UpdatesManager reloaded directly on resume when an update was pending. Settings' manual check also downloads, and the new effect now raises the screen for that download as well.
contracts.before_after: Before: silent reload on resume after a long absence. After: a modal asks first. Each update is offered once (`lastOffered` ref); "Not now" holds until a different update or a long absence.
contracts.visible_effect: A full-screen modal appears whenever isUpdatePending turns true, at any point in the session.
contracts.failure_mode: The effect marks the update as offered even if showUpdateReady was ignored because a restart was under way. That is harmless. `lastOffered` is a ref, so it resets only when the manager remounts.

summary:
**Batch 1 of 2.** Part 1 replaces the silent OTA reload with a mascot screen and an opt-in restart that remembers the current page. The logic is clean and the pure modules are well tested. I found one real problem. The resume route is deleted at launch but only used once `config` is non-null, which an unreachable machine delays indefinitely, and the 2-minute age limit is not rechecked, so the page can open late or replace the one the user navigated to. Two smaller items: `applyUpdate` can run twice on a double tap, and the hidden buttons stay reachable by VoiceOver on iOS.

**Batch 2 of 2.** The test file for the update-screen state module has one vacuous test: \"never reloads on its own\" asserts on a mock that nothing can call. The other tests match the behaviour in `updateScreenState.ts`. The shared module-level state is reset between tests by `afterEach`. I found no other defects in this file. I added no contract entries for it.
